pll1d46c3-d1e3509.summary: Asks, since all goods happen by God's will, whether all evils, that is sins, happen by God's will or against it.

pll1d46c3-d1e3512.summary: Notes divided opinions: some say God wills evils to be or happen but not that he wills evils; others that he wills neither. Both agree God does not will evils, and each relies on authorities and reasons.
claims: All agree God does not will evils.

pll1d46c3-d1e3517.summary: Gives the first view's argument: if God willed evils not to be and could not prevent them, something would resist his will and he would be impotent like us; since he is omnipotent, evils can happen only by his will ('who resists his will?').

pll1d46c3-d1e3532.summary: Adds: Augustine said 'it must happen if he wills'; God either wills evils to happen or not; if not, they do not happen; they do happen; so he wills them to happen.

pll1d46c3-d1e3547.summary: Adds: it is good that evils exist or happen, or the supremely good would not permit them.

pll1d46c3-d1e3550.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: though evils as evils are not good, it is good that there be evils as well as goods; otherwise the omnipotent Good, for whom not permitting is as easy as doing, would not permit them; denying this endangers our confession of the Father almighty.
claims: It is good that evils exist.
God permits evils only because it is good to do so.

pll1d46c3-d1e3570.summary: Draws their conclusion: it is good that evils exist, God is author of all good and wills all good that is, so he wills evils to be or happen.

pll1d46c3-d1e3573.summary: Gives the second view: God neither wills evils to happen nor wills them not to happen (nor nills them), but only does not will them to happen. If he willed them, he would make them and be their author, which the saints deny.
claims: God does not will evils to happen.
If he did, he would be their author.

pll1d46c3-d1e3581.summary: Continues: if he willed evils not to happen and they happened, he would not be omnipotent. So they grant neither that God wills evils to happen (lest he be author) nor that he wills them not to happen (lest he seem impotent), but only that he does not will them to happen, showing him permitter, not author.
claims: God is permitter, not author, of evils.

pll1d46c3-d1e3584.summary: Supports this with John 1:3: 'all things were made through him' shows him author of all goods; 'without him was made nothing' denies him author of evils, that is, sin.
claims: God is author of all goods, not of sin.

pll1d46c3-d1e3605.summary: Explains that John did not say sin was made through him or against his will, but without him, that is, without his will. Evils happen neither with God willing nor nilling, but with him not willing; it is not subject to his will that evil happen or not, but that he permit it, since permitting evils is good. He wills to permit, not the evils, since evils are not good nor is it good that they exist.
claims: Sin is made without God's will.
God wills to permit evils, not the evils.
It is not good that evils happen.

pl-l1d46c3.summary: Asks whether evils, that is sins, happen by God's will or against it. Opinions differ: some say God wills evils to be or happen though he does not will evils; others say he neither wills them to be nor to happen; both agree God does not will evils. The first argue: if God willed evils not to happen and they did, he would be impotent; Augustine says what God wills must happen; and Augustine says it is good that evils exist, or the omnipotent Good would not permit them, and God wills all good. The second say God neither wills evils to happen (or he would be their author) nor wills them not to happen (or he would be impotent), but only does not will them to happen, being permitter, not author. 'Without him was made nothing' (John 1:3) means sin was made without his will. God wills to permit evils, but does not will evils, nor is it good that they happen.
claims: Opinions differ on whether God wills evils to happen.
All agree God does not will evils.
One view: God wills evils to happen, since otherwise he would be impotent, and it is good that evils exist.
Another view: God neither wills evils to happen nor wills them not to happen, but only does not will them.
God is permitter, not author, of evils.
'Without him was made nothing' means sin is made without God's will.
God wills to permit evils, not the evils themselves.
